claims: Artemis II is NASA’s 10-day crewed flight test.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than September 2025.
Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II marks the first human mission to lunar vicinity since 1972.
Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
The crew of Artemis II includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission will fly approximately 4,700 miles (7,600 km) beyond the Moon's far side.
The Artemis II mission surpasses previous crewed flight distances.
The primary goal of Artemis II is to demonstrate that Orion’s life-support systems can keep astronauts safe during a deep-space journey.
Artemis II will make Victor Glover the first person of color to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II will make Christina Koch the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II will make Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
The Artemis II crew will manually pilot the Orion spacecraft in Earth's orbit to assess its handling.
The Artemis II mission will perform a 'scenic loop' around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew will photograph and study terrain that has not been closely examined in over 50 years.
The Artemis II team will perform ongoing medical tests.
The Artemis II team will monitor the crew’s health in deep space.
The original designation of Artemis II is Exploration Mission-2 (EM-2).
Artemis II is commonly compared to 21st Century Apollo 8 due to similar orbit mission profile.
The SLS (Space Launch System) is the 32-story rocket lifting the Artemis II crew.
The Orion spacecraft for Artemis II is named Integrity.
The European Service Module (ESM-2) powers, propels, and sustains the spacecraft for Artemis II.
